results.references:
- Mingrui Liu and Tianbao Yang. [Adaptive Accelerated Gradient Converging Methods under Hölderian Error Bound Condition](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1611.07609v2). 2017 (NIPS publication; preprint first posted 2016, version used: May 2017). Complexity: $O(1+\sqrt{\kappa}\log^2(2\kappa)\log(2\kappa LR^2/\varepsilon))$ exact-gradient calls for adaAGC to obtain $f(x)-f_*\le\varepsilon$, including initialization and gradient tests; $\kappa=L/\mu\ge1$, $0<\varepsilon\le LR^2$, initial error-bound estimate $c_0=L^{-1/2}$ and doubling factor $2$.
- Olivier Fercoq and Zheng Qu. [Adaptive restart of accelerated gradient methods under local quadratic growth condition](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1709.02300v1). 2019 (IMA Journal of Numerical Analysis; version used: September 2017 preprint). Complexity: $O(1+\sqrt{\kappa}\log(2\kappa^2 LR^2/\varepsilon))$ exact-gradient calls for AdaRES to obtain $f(x)-f_*\le\varepsilon$, including initialization and restart tests; $\kappa=L/\mu\ge1$, $0<\varepsilon\le LR^2$, initial normalized growth estimate $1$.

problem_class.label: convex
problem_class.details: Unconstrained minimization of a globally convex, differentiable function f:E→ℝ with L-Lipschitz gradient, L>0. A minimizer exists within distance R≥0 of x0. Strong convexity is not assumed.

oracle.label: exact_gradient
oracle.details: Each query x returns ∇f(x) exactly, for every history and oracle seed. No function values are supplied. Each gradient query counts as one oracle call.
oracle.evidence: LongTails/Setups/SmoothConvexQuadraticGrowth.lean: spec.Query, spec.Reply and spec.admissible; LongTails/Template.lean: Oracle.answer and executeWithTrace.

distinctive_assumptions.label: quadratic_growth
distinctive_assumptions.details: Global quadratic growth with μ>0: for every x there exists a minimizer z such that (μ/2)‖x−z‖²≤f(x)−f(z). The minimizer may depend on x.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/SmoothConvexQuadraticGrowth.lean: spec.valid and final conjunct of spec.admissible.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: E is an arbitrary real Hilbert space, without a finite-dimensional restriction. Only E, L and x0 are public; μ, R and ε are hidden. Allowed algorithms use one predetermined sequence ηt>0 in xt+1=xt−ηt∇f(xt), independent of the hidden parameters, and output the current iterate.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/SmoothConvexQuadraticGrowth.lean: Public, Params, spec.publicInput, gradientMethod and spec.allowedAlgorithm; LongTails/Template.lean: Convergence.makeAlgorithm.

accuracy.label: objective_gap
accuracy.details: For ε>0, the final iterate after the supplied fixed gradient-call budget must satisfy f(output)−f(xstar)≤ε for a global minimizer xstar.
accuracy.evidence: LongTails/Setups/SmoothConvexQuadraticGrowth.lean: spec.successful and gradientMethod.output; LongTails/Template.lean: Convergence and execute.

accuracy.label: almost_sure
accuracy.details: The objective-gap inequality holds almost surely under the joint algorithm and oracle seed law.

setup_category.label: non_standard
setup_category.reason: The objective and quadratic-growth condition are classical. The additional requirement of a predetermined positive-step gradient sequence, independent of μ, R and ε, with final-iterate accuracy at an externally specified fixed budget makes this formulation a meaningful restricted variant.
